daily_reality.summary: Fire protection engineers research fire causes, design fire prevention/suppression systems, review building plans for code compliance, and investigate fire incidents. They work across consulting firms, government agencies, insurance companies, and industrial facilities.
typical_tasks: Review building plans for fire code compliance (NFPA, IBC)
Design fire sprinkler, suppression, and alarm systems
Conduct fire safety inspections of buildings during construction and occupancy
Perform fire risk assessments and hazard analyses
Investigate fire sites and determine system failures
Prepare technical reports on fire protection systems
Advise on fire prevention codes and standards development
Witness acceptance tests for fire protection systems
Evaluate new fire protection products, materials, and equipment
Coordinate with architects, contractors, and fire marshals
key_documents: Fire and life safety code compliance reviews

deadlines.nfpa_code_cycle: 3-year revision cycle for most NFPA standards
deadlines.fire_investigation: Reports typically within 30-90 days of incident

daily_reality.seasonality: Construction seasons (spring-fall) bring peak plan review and inspection work. Year-end budget deadlines drive project completions. Code edition updates (e.g., 2026 NFPA cycle) create periodic compliance review surges.

regulatory.summary: Governed by NFPA codes (300+ standards), International Building Code (IBC), and state/local fire codes. PE licensure in Fire Protection is critical for career advancement. 2026 NFPA updates require risk assessments to be directed by registered PEs.

key_laws.name: NFPA 13 — Standard for Installation of Sprinkler Systems
key_laws.description: Primary standard for automatic fire sprinkler system design and installation

key_laws.name: NFPA 72 — National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code
key_laws.description: Standards for fire alarm and emergency communication systems

key_laws.name: NFPA 101 — Life Safety Code
key_laws.description: Addresses building construction, protection, and occupancy features to minimize fire danger

key_laws.name: NFPA 25 — Inspection, Testing, and Maintenance
key_laws.description: Standards for water-based fire protection system ITM

key_laws.name: International Building Code (IBC)
key_laws.description: Model building code adopted by most US jurisdictions, includes fire safety provisions

requirements: ABET-accredited engineering degree (fire protection, mechanical, civil, or related)
Pass PE Fire Protection exam ($400, computer-based, once per year)
State PE license application and approval
licensing.pe_premium: Licensed PEs earn 36% more on average
licensing.nfpa_2026_update: 2026 NFPA codes now require risk assessment design to be directed by a registered design professional (PE) experienced in fire protection engineering

regulatory.penalties: Non-compliance with fire codes can result in stop-work orders, building closure, fines, and criminal liability in case of fire deaths. PE stamp misuse carries license revocation.

tools.summary: Fire protection engineers use specialized sprinkler design software, BIM tools, fire modeling programs, and hydraulic calculation tools for system design and code compliance analysis.

primary_tools.description: Purpose-built fire sprinkler system design software with Revit/BIM integration

primary_tools.name: SprinkCAD / SprinkCALC
primary_tools.description: Comprehensive sprinkler system design, hydraulic calculation, and fabrication software

primary_tools.name: Autodesk Revit (MEP/Fire Protection)
primary_tools.description: BIM platform for 3D fire protection system modeling and coordination

primary_tools.name: MicroBIM Fire
primary_tools.description: Professional fire design software for Revit — modeling, hydraulic calculations, fabrication

primary_tools.name: FDS (Fire Dynamics Simulator)
primary_tools.description: NIST computational fluid dynamics tool for fire modeling and smoke movement

primary_tools.name: Pathfinder / EVACNET
primary_tools.description: Egress modeling and evacuation simulation software

secondary_tools: Navisworks — BIM coordination and clash detection
Revizto — issue tracking and BIM collaboration
Microsoft Excel — hydraulic calculations and data analysis
Bluebeam Revu — PDF plan review markup
NFPA code books and online access (nfpa.org)
pain_points: Coordinating fire protection models with other MEP trades in BIM
Keeping up with NFPA code revision cycles (300+ standards)
Integration between sprinkler design software and general BIM tools
Legacy projects without existing digital documentation

terminology.summary: Fire protection engineering terminology revolves around NFPA standards, sprinkler system types, fire suppression methods, and code compliance classifications.

terms.NFPA: National Fire Protection Association — publisher of 300+ fire safety codes/standards
terms.AHJ: Authority Having Jurisdiction — local code enforcement body
terms.NICET: National Institute for Certification in Engineering Technologies
terms.wet system: Sprinkler system with water-filled pipes, ready for immediate discharge
terms.dry system: Sprinkler pipes filled with pressurized air/nitrogen, water released when sprinkler activates
terms.pre-action: Sprinkler system requiring two triggers (detection + sprinkler head activation)
terms.deluge: System where all sprinkler heads are open, flooding entire area simultaneously
terms.clean agent: Gaseous fire suppression (FM-200, Novec) that leaves no residue
terms.hydraulic calculation: Mathematical analysis of water flow and pressure in sprinkler piping
terms.commodity class: NFPA 13 classification of stored materials (Class I-IV) by fire vulnerability
terms.standpipe: Permanently installed piping for firefighter hose connections (NFPA 14)
terms.egress: Means of escape from a building during fire emergency
terms.fire load: Total combustible material in a given area
terms.ESFR: Early Suppression Fast Response — high-output ceiling sprinklers for storage

career_psychology.summary: Niche engineering specialty with strong demand and above-average salaries ($85K-$120K median). PE licensure is a career-defining milestone. The field offers meaningful work protecting lives but involves pressure from code complexity and liability.
career_path: Bachelor's degree in Fire Protection Engineering (only 3 ABET-accredited programs in US: UMD, WPI, OSU)
Or related engineering degree (mechanical, civil) with fire protection focus
PE in Fire Protection (after 4 years experience)
Senior Fire Protection Engineer / Project Manager
fears: Design failure leading to fire deaths and legal liability
Missing a code requirement in plan review
PE license revocation due to errors
Keeping up with 300+ NFPA standards and revision cycles
Scope creep and project budget overruns
motivation: Directly protecting lives and property from fire
Intellectually challenging work combining engineering and codes
Niche specialty with high demand and low competition
Above-average engineering salaries with PE premium
Variety of project types (buildings, industrial, healthcare)
burnout_factors: Complex regulatory landscape with constantly evolving codes
High liability and pressure of life-safety responsibilities
Plan review backlogs in high-demand markets
Limited number of FPE programs creating talent shortages

community.summary: Tight-knit professional community centered around SFPE (5,000+ members, 120+ chapters worldwide) and NFPA, with regular conferences, technical publications, and local chapter networking.

associations.name: Society of Fire Protection Engineers (SFPE)
associations.description: World's leading professional society for FPE, 5,000+ members, 120+ chapters, 20+ student chapters

associations.name: National Fire Protection Association (NFPA)
associations.description: Publisher of 300+ fire safety codes/standards, certifications, training

associations.name: National Society of Professional Engineers (NSPE)
associations.description: Broader PE advocacy, joint positions with SFPE on FPE qualifications

associations.name: NICET — National Institute for Certification in Engineering Technologies
associations.description: Technical certifications for fire protection system designers and inspectors

online_communities: SFPE local chapter events and webinars
LinkedIn SFPE and fire protection groups
conferences: SFPE Annual Conference & Expo (400+ professionals globally)
SFPE Europe Conference on Fire Safety Engineering
community.key_publication: SFPE Handbook of Fire Protection Engineering — authoritative reference

market.summary: Niche but growing specialty with strong demand due to limited FPE graduates and increasing code complexity. Median salaries range $85K-$120K. PE licensure significantly boosts earning potential (36% premium).
market.growth_rate: 4% projected growth (aligned with Health & Safety Engineers category)
top_employers: Fire protection engineering consulting firms (Jensen Hughes, Arup, Rolf Jensen)
Large MEP firms with FPE divisions
Industrial facilities (oil & gas, manufacturing, data centers)
market_trends: Talent shortage due to only 3 ABET-accredited FPE programs in US
2026 NFPA code updates requiring PE oversight for risk assessments
Growing energy storage (lithium-ion) fire safety demand
Mass timber construction creating new fire engineering challenges
Data center boom driving fire suppression system demand
